newsitem.title: GERMANY: Publisher promotes Europrice books, level taxes.
newsitem.headline: Publisher promotes Europrice books, level taxes.

text.p: Books could be sold at Europrices across the continent once a universal tax system has produced a level playing field, a leading publisher said on Friday.
"The pressures to harmonise national book pricing systems will inevitably remain, particularly after monetary union," said John Clement, President of the Federation of European Publishers.

"English language books, which are widely distributed throughout all European markers, may in future carry uniform fixed Europrices, if not in Britain, in most other countries," he told Publishing News at the world's biggest book fair which has attracted 9,200 publishers from 110 countries.
Britain abolished price fixing last year. The Net Book Agreement fell apart after three leading publishers dropped out. Supermarkets and stores were then hit by a flurry of discounting.
But tax rates on books vary widely across the continent.

"The battle to establish zero-rate VAT (Value Added Tax) on books throughout Europe as an essential prop to literary culture and understanding is probably the single toughest issue the federation faces," Clement said.
